newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire wants say on composition of foreign force.
newsitem.headline: Zaire wants say on composition of foreign force.

text.p: Zaire on Friday insisted on the right to challenge the composition of the planned international force that is to deploy in the war-ravaged east of the Central African country.
Government spokesman Boguo Makeli told Reuters that Zaire wanted to be formally consulted before the force, due to be approved by the U.N. Security Council on Friday, was deployed.
"We reserve the right to be able to challenge any state having links with the aggressors and those who have shown hostility in the past," he said. "We have not yet been consulted."
Boguo declined to specify countries that would be considered undesirable and said his government had not yet received a list of those that might take part.
Zaire has in the past criticised both the United States and South Africa for selling military equipment to Rwanda.
Chaos has reigned along Zaire's eastern frontier since the army was driven back by a coalition of Tutsi rebels and the Tutsi-dominated Rwandan army.
Zaire, which has the twin objectives of regaining lost territory and removing Rwandan Hutu refugees from its soil, wants the force to have a political as well as a humanitarian objective.
Zairean officials had no immediate comment on the return of tens of thousands of Hutus to Rwanda on Friday, simply restating earlier positions.
"We insist that aid be distributed only on the other side of the border. There can be no question of establishing new Rwandan refugee camps in Zaire," said Boguo.
